source_snapshot.procedure: In BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, check Chassis information and detail information.
source_snapshot.criteria: Data should be readable and correct.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES filters an assumed FirmwareInventory payload by names containing RETIMER, bypasses TLS verification, exposes credentials, does not follow collection/member links, and cannot prove eight indexed devices, physical/PCIe identity, active versus staged lifecycle or the required WebUI chassis details.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly restores vendor retimer topology, complete per-device firmware lifecycle, protected collection and a no-update boundary; once that read-only Project package exists, no point-of-action confirmation is required.

old_problem: A substring-matched firmware list was being over-credited as complete RETIMER_0~7 chassis evidence. The earlier review supplied the right topology/lifecycle model but retained a hybrid class solely for missing Project mapping and version expectations. Those are readiness inputs; this case performs no update, reset or PCIe write.
disposition_reason: Account for RETIMER_0 through RETIMER_7 independently, bind each logical index to an approved physical/PCIe/chassis identity, enumerate complete FirmwareInventory/SoftwareInventory member records, distinguish active/running, backup/staged and unsupported fields through the target's documented model, capture actual WebUI chassis/detail evidence and compare each device to the Project firmware matrix. All collection is protected and read-only.
decision_basis: XLSX row 950, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 951 were directly reviewed; next pending identity was verified as Functionality row 951 / variant 83f1846456011787.

The Items supplies eight explicit retimer indices and Procedure supplies chassis/detail presentation. A complete review must retain both physical/topology identity and per-device firmware detail rather than selecting a name-filtered inventory shortcut.

DMTF SoftwareInventory supplies component identity, Version, VersionScheme, Status and Updateable metadata, while Chassis provides physical/location/relationship context; vendor topology is still required to bind firmware records to RETIMER_0~7.

Installed, active/running, backup and staged records are not universally equivalent. The target-advertised schema and approved vendor lifecycle map determine which record satisfies the expected running version, with unsupported/null kept explicit.

ED-02, ED-14, ED-21, ED-26 and ED-33 through ED-38 preserve every indexed device and lifecycle identity, forbid name/count extrapolation, separate inventory from update coverage and allow safe Project parameterization.

test_case.test_name: Validate RETIMER_0 through RETIMER_7 topology and active/staged firmware lifecycle independently
test_case.purpose: Verify that every Project-supported RETIMER_0 through RETIMER_7 position is independently accounted, uniquely bound to the intended chassis/PCIe retimer, exposes complete readable firmware identity/lifecycle/health data matching the approved recipe, appears correctly in the actual BMC WebUI, and is observed without any firmware, PCIe, reset or power mutation.
required_package: Immutable BMC/platform/firmware/WebUI identity, trusted TLS chain, protected read-only credentials and topology/serial redaction rules
Approved RETIMER_0~7 logical-to-physical map including chassis/service label, PCIe root/slot/path or vendor durable identity and expected present/unfitted/unsupported positions
Service-root-discovered UpdateService FirmwareInventory or vendor-approved SoftwareInventory collection, supported schema versions, pagination and complete member access

Per-retimer expected firmware matrix: component identity, active/running version, allowed backup/staged version, VersionScheme, Status.State/Health, Updateable expectation and vendor lifecycle semantics
Authoritative association method between each firmware inventory member and the physical/PCIe retimer; name substring alone is not authoritative
Actual WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs retimer chassis/detail field mapping, freshness tolerance and evidence/redaction storage
test_case.test_command: READ ONLY. Verify immutable target; discover UpdateService/FirmwareInventory and relevant Chassis or vendor topology resources from the Redfish service root. Traverse complete pagination and every member `@odata.id`, preserving redacted raw JSON; a case-insensitive RETIMER name filter may only locate candidates and may not establish identity. Using the approved durable relationships/topology, bind each actual component uniquely to RETIMER_0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 7 and record authoritative unfitted/unsupported positions. For every present device, normalize Id/Name, durable chassis/PCIe relationship, Version, VersionScheme, SoftwareId when supported, Status.State/Health, Updateable, ReleaseDate and vendor active/running versus backup/staged role. Open the actual WebUI Inventory and LEDs retimer/chassis table and each detail view, capture timestamped visual evidence, and reconcile index, physical identity, lifecycle/version and health with API and the Project matrix. Keep absent, duplicate, extra, unknown/null, unsupported, stale and failed reads distinct. Repeat only read-only fingerprints. Do not use `curl -k`, process-visible credentials, UpdateService actions, SoftwareInventory.Activate, firmware upload/update/rollback, retimer reset, PCIe writes, power actions or log clearing.
test_case.expected_result: All eight logical positions are independently accounted with no duplicate mapping. Every expected present retimer has one durable physical/PCIe identity and complete schema-valid inventory whose active/running version and health match the approved recipe; backup/staged records are separately labeled and match their own expected state rather than being mistaken for running firmware. Documented unfitted/unsupported positions use the approved representation, actual WebUI records reconcile to each device, no unexpected/missing/extra component exists and pre/post/audit evidence proves no firmware, PCIe, reset or power change.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires RETIMER_0~7 accounting, unique topology binding, complete collection/member traversal, explicit lifecycle interpretation, exact per-device expected-version/health comparison and actual WebUI visual parity. A substring filter, count, version-only list or eight similar names cannot pass. Missing/duplicate/extra device, wrong PCIe mapping, staged version credited as running, unexplained null/unknown/unsupported, UI/API mismatch or incomplete Project matrix is FAIL or NOT READY by policy. Unfitted/unsupported is acceptable only with authoritative applicability evidence; missing topology/version inputs are NOT READY, not Engineering Decision Pending.
safety_gate: Use only certificate-verified protected GET/read operations discovered from the service root; do not use `curl -k`, expose credentials or infer identity solely from a name substring.
Keep this case strictly inventory-only. Never invoke UpdateService, SoftwareInventory.Activate, firmware upload/update/rollback, retimer reset, PCIe control, power or log-clear actions.
Bind every logical index to an approved durable physical/PCIe/chassis identity and stop on ambiguity, duplication or cross-SUT mapping; do not extrapolate one component to siblings.
Separate active/running, backup, staged and unsupported lifecycle records using documented target semantics; do not choose the highest or first version heuristically.
Distinguish documented unfitted/unsupported from missing inventory, omitted response, unauthorized request and transport failure; none may be silently accepted.
Redact sensitive topology/serial identifiers while retaining stable per-index tokens, links, timestamps and raw hashes required for audit.
expected_evidence: Target BMC/platform/WebUI/schema identity, trusted session, complete paginated FirmwareInventory/SoftwareInventory collection and approved RETIMER_0~7 topology/population map
Complete raw redacted per-member records and durable chassis/PCIe association evidence for every present retimer
Normalized eight-position matrix with active/running, backup/staged, Version/VersionScheme, Status/Health, Updateable and exact Project comparison
Actual WebUI retimer/chassis table/detail visual artifacts with per-index topology/lifecycle/API parity and freshness timestamps
Pre/post read-only fingerprints, preserved audit/log evidence, strict no-update/no-reset/no-PCIe-write proof and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is intended. On wrong target, incomplete pagination, ambiguous topology, unknown lifecycle, credential exposure or UI/API mismatch, stop collection, preserve/redact evidence and close the session. Do not activate, update, roll back, reset or retrain any retimer to clarify inventory; obtain the authoritative vendor topology/lifecycle mapping.

source_conflict.reason: Items' indexed retimer target and Procedure's chassis/detail view are complementary. DeepSeek's firmware-name shortcut is incomplete recommendation logic, not a competing Master purpose.

blocked.reason: The eight-device read-only purpose is clear. Physical/PCIe topology, lifecycle semantics and expected versions are finite Project readiness inputs.
